old_title: Live: Ukraine backers gather as Russian attacks escalate, air defence runs low
new_title: Zelensky calls on allies to cover €27 billion gap for Ukraine's air defence needs
old_text:
Live: Ukraine backers gather as Russian attacks escalate, air defence runs low
Ukraine on Monday hosts a meeting of its key European backers to press for air-defence supplies and more pressure on Moscow, with Russian attacks killing more civilians than at any time since the first months of the invasion. The meeting of the Coalition of the Willing will be jointly chaired by the leaders of Britain, France and Germany. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.
Zelensky, on Ukraine's independence day, says Ukraine wants peace but 'will not just give in'
Germany's Wadephul to urge Rubio to take more active role on Ukraine
German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul plans to speak to his US counterpart, Marco Rubio, by phone to urge him to become more personally involved in diplomatic efforts related to the war in Ukraine, he told radio broadcaster Deutschlandfunk.
Wadephul, who was recently in Ukraine, told the broadcaster that US diplomacy had so far been handled largely by presidential envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff.
"I may be able to encourage him (Rubio) myself to do more there," the German minister said, adding that Berlin was pursuing other channels to help restart negotiations.
Ukraine hit Russian fighter aircraft, two vessels in Black Sea
The Ukrainian military struck a Russian MIG-29 fighter aircraft and two Russian vessels in Black Sea overnight, Ukraine's drone forces commander Robert Brovdi said.
Brovdi said on the Telegram app that one of the vessels attacked was a tanker, and the other was a bulk carrier.
EU approves further €6.1 billion for Ukraine's defence
The European Commission approved a further €6.1 billion ($7.12 billion) in financial aid for Ukraine to procure new defence systems, such as air defence, missiles, ammunition and radars.
The EU said this latest aid package came on top of €16 billion of previously approved procurement plans, of which €8.35 billion had already been disbursed.
"As Russia intensifies its attacks, we are stepping up to help Ukraine protect its people and defend its skies. Europe stands with Ukraine and we will deliver what it needs, when it needs it," said European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen in a statement.
EU's Costa, UK's Burnham arrive in Ukraine for independence day
European Council President Antonio Costa and UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham arrived in the Ukrainian capital Kyiv to mark the country's independence day, Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said.
The visiting dignitaries also included Luxembourg Prime Minister Luc Frieden, Moldova's President Maia Sandu and Estonia's President Alar Karis, Sybiha said on X, posting photos of the officials arriving at the Kyiv station.
Russia downs 351 Ukrainian drones overnight, defence ministry says
The Russian Defence Ministry said its forces had intercepted and destroyed 351 Ukrainian drones overnight over a number of regions.
Russia says its forces hit tanker carrying fuel near Ukraine's Odesa
The Russian Defence Ministry said it had hit a tanker carrying fuel and lubricants for Ukrainian troops in the port of Pivdennyi near Odesa, as well as port infrastructure facilities used for unloading and storing military cargo.
Zelensky rejects rival's call for elections
Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky has rejected the prospect of wartime elections, saying it would be highly dangerous.
Analysis by FRANCE 24 international affairs editor Matthew-Mary Caruchet.
Ukraine keeps up attacks on Russian e-commerce giant Ozon
Russian e-commerce giant Ozon said that its warehouses came under drone attack, as Ukraine pressed ahead with its campaign targeting logistics sites.
Kyiv has for weeks mounted a campaign targeting Russia's Wildberries - the country's top online retailer - alleging it supplied components to the military.
Ozon is Russia's second-largest online marketplace, with its pick-up points and delivery boxes ubiquitous across the country.
New UK PM Andy Burnham to make visit to Kyiv
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham will visit Kyiv on his first international visit since taking office last month, his office said, as Ukraine marks its 35th independence anniversary.
Burnham has vowed to give strong support to Ukraine as it battles Russia's invasion.
The Labour Party leader's visit comes as he announced that Britain had "agreed that defence firm MBDA can release classified information on UK components for the long-range missile, SCALP, to establish local assembly lines in Ukraine", a statement said.
Zelensky says war time elections in Ukraine would 'destroy the country'
In remarks on Sunday, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky spoke out against holding war time elections, saying it would be too dangerous for the country and would "split" Ukraine.
The remarks come in response to a call from the former defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov to organise a vote, after he was fired by Zelensky last month.
Details and analysis by FRANCE 24 correspondent in Kyiv, Emmanuelle Chaze.
Russia's Ozon says Dagestan logistics hub on fire after drone attack
Russian online retailer Ozon's logistics hub in Makhachkala in Dagestan was on fire after a drone attack, it said on the Telegram messaging app.
The company has also temporarily shut down two warehouses in the nearby regions of Stavropol and Adygeya in the North Caucasus amid a drone attack alert, it said, though they were not damaged.
North Korea preparing further Russia troop deployments, no sign move imminent, Seoul says
South Korea's Defence Ministry said North Korea was continuing preparations for an additional troop deployment to Russia, but had detected no signs that such a deployment was imminent, according to a South Korean lawmaker's office.
The assessment came after North Korea's Kim Yo Jong, sister of leader Kim Jong Un, last week denied Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky's claim that Pyongyang planned to send up to 50,000 more troops to Russia to fight for its ally.
South Korea's Defence Ministry said in a statement to lawmaker Yu Yong-weon that North Korea had continued to supply Russia with weapons systems, including short-range ballistic missiles, according to Yu's office.
Drone debris kills two children in Russia's Krasnodar, governor says
Two children were killed and another nine people, including seven children, were injured after drone debris hit a private childcare center in Krasnodar in southern Russia overnight, Governor Veniamin Kondratyev said on the Telegram messaging app.
Debris also fell on apartment buildings in the city, causing a fire at warehouses, he said, without providing details.
Ukraine backers gather as war escalates, air defence runs low
Ukraine on Monday hosts a meeting of its key European backers to press for critical air-defence supplies and more pressure on Moscow, with Russian attacks killing more civilians than at any time since the first months of the invasion.
The meeting of the Coalition of the Willing will be jointly chaired by the leaders of Britain, France and Germany.
UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham will be in Kyiv for his first international trip since entering 10 Downing Street, and several other leaders are expected to join remotely.
Welcome to the FRANCE 24 liveblog covering the war in Ukraine and diplomatic efforts to end the conflict.
(FRANCE 24 with AFP, AP and Reuters)
new_text:
Zelensky calls on allies to cover €27 billion gap for Ukraine's air defence needs
President Volodymyr Zelensky on Monday urged Ukraine's allies to help cover a funding gap of €27 billion for its air defence needs in 2026. Ukraine is hosting a meeting of its key European backers in Kyiv as the country marks its 35th Independence Day. Read about the day's events as they unfolded on our liveblog.
This live page is no longer being updated. For more of our coverage of the war in Ukraine, click here.
UK, France 're-announce' anti-missile technology for Ukraine: 'None will be online for years'
Annette Young is pleased to welcome Dr. Frank Ledwidge, former military intelligence officer and Senior Lecturer in Strategy at Portsmouth University. According to Dr. Ledwidge, the latest European commitments to Ukraine are merely politically symbolic. He warns that the coalition is failing to address Kyiv's most urgent problem: air defence. Ukraine needs interceptors capable of defeating Russian ballistic and hypersonic missiles, The war-torn country remains exposed to attacks on its defence industry and Russia's ruthless campaign against civil energy infrastructure as winter approaches.
Ukraine to give Britain battlefield data in AI deal
Ukraine will give Britain access to an AI dataset containing millions of battlefield images, the UK government said Monday, in a deal London said would help it protect military bases and other sites.
The dataset, known as "Avengers", is currently used to train autonomous Ukrainian drones.
Describing the data as a "goldmine", London said it could eventually use the dataset to "protect airports, prisons and even railways and energy plants", without elaborating.
Signed by British Prime Minister Andy Burnham and Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky in Kyiv on Monday, the deal offers Ukraine expertise from British researchers and universities in return.
The partnership will "bring together Ukraine's unrivalled operational experience with Britain's world-class AI ecosystem," Burnham said in a statement.
Russia says it struck cargo vessel in Ukraine's Odesa port
Russian forces struck a cargo vessel in Ukraine's Black Sea port of Odesa on Monday, Russia's Defence
Ministry said.
The ministry did not identify the vessel but said it had delivered what it described as a military cargo.
The claim could not be independently verified.
Ukraine showing 'remarkable innovation': Kyiv 'holding front line' while striking Russia's economy
Genie Godula is pleased to welcome Samantha de Bendern, Associate Fellow at Chatham House. Europe is taking increasingly consequential steps to support Ukraine, but de Bendern warns that they remain insufficient to address the country's fundamental vulnerability. Are Ukraine's allies prepared to actively help protect Ukrainian airspace? That debate reaches back to the earliest weeks of the full-scale invasion: even after president Biden warned in 2022 of an imminent Russian attack, Kyiv's allies ruled out enforcing a no-fly zone, fearing that direct NATO engagement could escalate into a wider war with Moscow.
Russia's Perm oil refinery halted operations after August 21 drone attack, sources say
The Perm oil refinery, Russia's seventh-largest oil processing plant by volumes, stopped operations following a Ukrainian drone attack, which caused fire and damage to technological units on August 21, two industry sources said on Monday.
Ukraine has stepped up attacks on Russia's energy infrastructure, including oil refineries, in recent months to undermine Moscow's war efforts and cut its financial income.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Friday that Ukraine's military hit a Russian oil refinery in the city of Perm.
Numerous Russian regions have reported fuel shortages due to the strikes on the refineries and a robust seasonal demand.
Sources said that the primary CDU-4 unit, which accounts for almost 40% of the plant's capacity, was halted on August 21. It is able to process 14,000 metric tons of oil per day.
According to preliminary estimates, the repair works could take between one and two weeks.
Romania defence ministry says drone fragments found likely from earlier UAV breach
Romania's Defence Ministry said on Monday that drone fragments found on a property in Galați County most likely came from a drone detected earlier in the day and contained no explosive charge.
The ministry earlier said radar systems tracked intermittent aerial signals over Moldova before they appeared in the Târgu Bujor area of eastern Romania, prompting the scrambling of two F-16 fighter jets and a military helicopter.
NATO member Romania shares a 614 km (381 miles) land border with Ukraine and has reported repeated breaches of its airspace by Russian drones over the past four years.
EU accelerates rollout of Ukraine loan, Costa says
The EU is "accelerating" the rollout of its €90 billion ($105 billion) loan to Ukraine to support the
country's air defence and energy infrastructure, EU Council President Antonio Costa said on Monday.
"We will continue to support Ukraine for as long as necessary and provide Ukraine with security guarantees once this terrible war ends, so that it never happens again," Costa said in a post on X following a visit to Kyiv.
UK's Burnham urges allies to do 'everything' to support Ukraine's skies
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham urged allies on Monday to "do everything we can" and
"dig into our own stocks of air defence" to protect Ukraine against Russian attacks at his first meeting co-chairing the so-called Coalition of the Willing.
"(Russian President Vladimir) Putin is now hoping he can win through a campaign of terror using ballistic missiles against Ukrainian civilians ... This can never be the route to victory, and we need to be clear in sending that message," Burnham said at the start of the meeting.
"It means doing everything we can all do, and working with our allies as well, beyond this coalition, to dig into our own stocks of air defence ... to protect Ukraine from the missiles that are falling now."
He also said there was a need for more sanctions on Russian oil and LNG exports to ramp up the pressure on Moscow.
Zelensky urges allies to cover €27 billion gap for defence needs
President Volodymyr Zelensky urged Ukraine's allies to deliver an air defence package ahead of the
winter, with Russia expected to renew its strikes on his country's energy infrastructure.
Addressing a Coalition of the Willing meeting in Kyiv, Zelensky also asked Ukraine's partners to help cover a funding gap of €27 billion for its defence sector needs in 2026. In this context, the president reminded his allies of the Russian assets held frozen across European jurisdictions.
Vatican's top diplomat visits Moscow
The Vatican's most senior diplomat begins a visit to Russia on Monday, aimed at maintaining dialogue with Moscow against a background of particularly tense international relations.
Archbishop Paul Richard Gallagher, Secretary for Relations with States, is the most senior Vatican official to visit the country since the start of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.
Gallagher will hold talks on Tuesday with Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov.
The programme for his visit, which is due to last until Thursday, includes meetings with representatives of the Moscow Patriarchate and with the small, local Catholic community.
This visit, his first since November 2021, is in keeping with the Vatican's diplomatic tradition, which emphasises active neutrality and a refusal to break contact with parties to a conflict.
The Holy See is promoting humanitarian moves from the two sides such as prisoner exchanges or the repatriation of Ukrainian children while exploring opportunities for peace negotiations.
However, bilateral ties are delicate, particularly due to the alignment of the Orthodox Church and Patriarch Kirill with the Kremlin.
Putin hands Russian state right to take control of badly protected infrastructure objects
President Vladimir Putin on Monday handed the Russian state the authority to take control of critically-important infrastructure facilities if they are deemed to be poorly protected from Ukrainian drone attacks and other threats.
The special powers, set out in a presidential decree, will allow the state to take over temporary administration of such facilities at a time when Ukraine has stepped up drone attacks on oil refineries and retail warehouses.
The state will be able to take control of physical and financial assets and formal ownership rights if the entities responsible for such facilities are judged to have failed in their duty to protect them and are too slow to repair them after any attack, according to the decree.
It listed fuel, energy, industrial, communications, transport and logistics facilities and other objects regarded as critically-important for ensuring the security and economic stability of the state and the population as falling within the new decree's scope.
Putin last week ordered the government to launch a programme to rebuild commercial warehouses damaged or destroyed by Ukraine in recent weeks.
Kyiv has attacked at least two dozen warehouses belonging to Russia's top online retailer Wildberries since July 18, destroying a large chunk of its storage capacity.
Ukraine, Russia release 10 captives in prisoner swap
Ten Ukrainian prisoners of war who were thought to be missing in action have been released in a prisoner exchange, said President Volodymyr Zelensky.
He did not mention Russia in his statement, saying only that the prisoners had been released via Belarus, one of Moscow's closest allies.
"We are bringing back 10 of our warriors -- through Belarus. Servicemen of the Armed Forces and the National Guard of Ukraine. They defended the country in the Donetsk sector," Zelensky said in a post on X.
"All of them had been considered missing in action," he said, without giving further details.
Europe ramps up support to Ukraine as its US-dependent air defence runs low
European leaders are meeting in Kyiv as Ukraine holds celebrations for its 35th Independence Day.
The Coalition of the Willing is set to hold talks regarding support to the country, four-and-a-half years after the Russian invasion started, with the European Union having announced it was releasing over €6 billion in aid. But US support to Kyiv regarding critical air defence is still missing.
FRANCE 24's Kethevane Gorjestani tells us more.
Burnham says UK will continue aiding Ukraine despite Russia's 'outrageous threats'
The United Kingdom will continue providing defence aid to war-torn Ukraine despite Russia's "outrageous threats", UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said on a visit to Kyiv.
"Despite Russia's outrageous threats to my country, we will continue our support for Ukraine's defence," Burnham said in a speech delivered on the country's Independence Day and ahead of a meeting of its international backers.
Ukraine celebrates resilience on anniversary of its independence
Ukraine strikes Russian military plant in Rostov region
Ukraine's military struck a Russian military plant in the Rostov region overnight, causing a fire, the Ukrainian General Staff said.
The General Staff said on the Telegram messaging app that the Kamensky plant is producing rocket fuel ammunition and missile systems.
European leaders rally in Kyiv to celebrate Ukraine's Independence Day
European leaders joined President Volodymyr Zelensky in Kyiv for official celebrations marking Ukraine's Independence Day as Russia pushes on with its four-year-old invasion of the country.
Among the guests is new UK prime minister Andy Burnham, his first overseas trip since taking office in July.
FRANCE 24's Emmanuelle Chaze tells us more from Kyiv.
Russia says it has taken control of three more Ukrainian villages
Russia's Defence Ministry said that its forces have captured three more eastern Ukrainian villages.
In its daily briefing, the ministry named the villages as Kucheriv Yar in the Donetsk region, Dolynka in the Zaporizhzhia region, and Novokostiantynivka in the Sumy region.
Kremlin says new UK missile help for Ukraine 'adds fuel to the fire'
The Kremlin said that Britain's decision to hand Ukraine classified information on British-made components used to make SCALP long-range cruise missiles would "add fuel to the fire" and was regarded by Moscow extremely negatively.
Asked about UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham's visit to Kyiv and the new British missile support, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Britain was a participant in the war on Ukraine's side and accused London of doing everything it could to prevent any progress towards an eventual peace deal.
The Kremlin says it is working on support for businesses after Ozon warehouse strikes
The Kremlin, asked about the possibility of state support for online retailer Ozon, whose warehouses have been targeted by Ukrainian drones, said that the government is working with businesses on support in "a difficult situation".
(FRANCE 24 with AFP, AP and Reuters)
